4. The trial court, after hearing the partiers, perused the documents and other materials on record, decreed the suit in part, vide his judgment and decree dated 20-2-2006 [(decree signed on 26-2-2006) (Annexure-A)] allotting 0.03½  decimals of land to defendant Nos. 1, 3 and 4, based on 2(two) deeds of gift Ext. 2 and 2(Ka). Against the said judgment and decree of the trial court, the plaintiff had preferred Other Appeal No.166 of 2007 before the learned District Judge, Chattogram, which is now pending for hearing before the learned Additional District Judge, 6th Court, Chattogram. In the said appeal, the plaintiff has filed an application for amendment of the plaint on 13-4-2014 (Annexure-F). The contesting defendant filed written objection on 19-5-2014 (Annexure-G) against the said petition. The appellate court, after hearing both the parties on this issue of amendment of plaint, by it judgment and order dated 19-9-2016 has allowed the said application in part. 

 6. Learned Advocate Mr Sheikh Muhammed Serajul Islam appeared on behalf of the petitioner. His main contention is that, the original suit was filed in the year 1991, for partition. The trial court, after proper appreciation of the evidence on record, passed the preliminary decree allotting 0.03½  decimals of land in favour of the defendant Nos. 1, 3 and 4, based on two deeds of gift Ext. 2 and 2(Ka). He also submits that the plaintiff preferred appeal after occurring delay of 425 days alongwith an application for condonation of delay and the said delay was not condoned by the appellate court and this plaintiff then filed a Civil Revision No. 5620 of 2007 and, in the said revision, the Rule was made absolute, vide judgment and order dated 2-5-2013, after condoning the delay, and the High Court Division also directed the appellate court to dispose of the appeal within 3(three) months from the date of receipt of the order, but this plaintiff did not co-operate the appellate court in compliance with the order of the High Court Division, rather he resorted to dilatory tactic and, in furtherance of his intention, he has filed this application for amendment of the plaint, not with intent to have adjudicated the real controversies between the parties. The learned Advocate proceeds on that, the proposed amendment also amounts to setting aside the findings of the trial court, which is not contemplated under the provisions of Order VI, rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure. He also submits that, apart from this, the plaintiff even filed an application on 18-8-2014, before the appellate court for withdrawal of the original suit. In these circumstances, the learned Advocate submits that, the impugned order has been passed by the appellate court without at all appreciating these legal and factual aspects of this case and also he did not apply his judicial mind in passing the impugned order and that has resulted in error in the decision occasioning failure of justice and causing serious prejudice to the petitioner. He prayed for making the Rule absolute. 

 12. Purpose of filing this particular amendment petition is not to have the controversies determined, as contemplated in Rule 17 of Order VI of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, but to have the findings of the trial court nullified, after it has passed the judgment with specific findings. This application for amendment is, however, beyond the intent and scope of Order VI, rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, hence it is immaterial at what stage this application for amendment has been filed. Moreover, the plaintiff-opposite parties have filed another application for withdrawal of the suit on 18-8-2014, which also shows their malafidfe intention to nullify the judgment and decree of the trial court by frustrating the appeal.
